attribution_limitations: The case text states that the blood count, electrolytes, coagulation, inflammatory markers, liver and renal function, lipid profile, glycaemia, cardiac enzymes and thyroid hormones were within the respective reference ranges, while the printed Table 1 values for AST, cholesterol, LDL cholesterol, triglycerides and fT3 lie outside their printed ranges. Both are kept; table rows carry no flag from reference ranges, and the narrative statement is review_only.
The case report calls the alcohol exposure before the 2018 episode "occasional alcohol consumption", while the Conclusions call it a "considerable alcohol intake". The amount is not reconciled.

The Figure 4 caption calls the echocardiogram "baseline", while the text cites Figure 4 for the transthoracic echocardiogram performed the following day. The left atrial volume of 32 mL printed only in the caption is kept without a time. The bedside echocardiogram on admission also reported normal left atrial volumes without a value, so which examination the caption's "baseline" refers to is not fully settled; the value is linked to the following-day echocardiogram only through the text's Figure 4 citation.
Edoxaban is described as optional post-cardioversion anticoagulation at discharge; whether the patient took it is not stated.

The wording "denied any history of drug assumption" does not say whether medications or recreational drugs are meant; "nonsmoker" is not an explicit never-use statement. Both are kept as literal denials without further interpretation.
"showed or reported no recurrence of AF" does not separate objective rhythm documentation from patient report during the 1-year follow-up; kept as stated.
The trigeminocardiac reflex and vagal-induced PAF are authors' hedged interpretations ("likely", "we may speculate") and are not recorded as established causes or diagnoses.

He had rapid irregular palpitations, and the onset followed a transient sinus bradycardia during sampling.
